cases.sentence: ___ вваливался в черно-бурой лисе, сверкая миллионом снежных блесток.
options: хозяин
хозяина
хозяину
хозяином
cases.translation: The master came barging in wearing his silver fox fur coat, sparkling with a million snowflakes.
cases.explain: «Хозяин вваливался» — the master is the subject of the verb вваливался, so he stands in the Nominative.

cases.sentence: Запах от блюда шёл такой, что рот ___ немедленно наполнился жидкой слюной.
options: пёс
пса
псу
псом
cases.translation: The smell from the dish was such that the dog's mouth immediately filled with drool.
cases.explain: «Рот (кого?) пса» — possession is expressed by the Genitive case, so пёс becomes пса.

cases.sentence: Приёма сегодня не было потому, что, как известно, по ___ приёма не бывает, и божество сидело в кабинете, развернув на столе какие-то тяжёлые книги с пёстрыми картинками.
options: вторник
вторника
вторникам
вторником
cases.translation: There were no patients today because, as is known, there are no patients on ___, and the deity was sitting in his office with some heavy books with colorful pictures spread out on the table.
cases.explain: The preposition «по» expressing a recurring day governs the Dative case, so вторник becomes вторникам.

cases.sentence: Бедняга наголодался, – Филипп Филиппович на конце вилки подал псу закуску, принятую тем с фокусной ловкостью, и ___ с грохотом свалил в полоскательницу.
options: вилка
вилки
вилке
вилку
cases.translation: Poor fellow was starved, Filipp Filippovich held out a treat to the dog on the end of a fork, taken by him with trick-like dexterity, and ___ fell with a crash into the rinsing bowl.
cases.explain: The transitive verb «свалил» (tossed/dropped) takes a direct object in the Accusative, so вилка becomes вилку.

cases.sentence: Через два дня он уже лежал рядом с ___ углей и смотрел, как работает Дарья Петровна.
options: корзина
корзины
корзине
корзиной
cases.translation: Two days later he was already lying next to the basket of coals, watching Darya Petrovna work.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» meaning "next to/alongside" governs the Instrumental case here, so корзина becomes корзиной.

cases.sentence: Филипп Филиппович, откинувшись, позвонил, и в вишнёвой ___ появилась Зина.
options: портьера
портьеры
портьеру
портьере
cases.translation: Filipp Filippovich leaned back and rang the bell, and Zina appeared in the cherry-red curtain doorway.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» expressing location governs the Prepositional case, so портьера becomes портьере.

reading.ru: Запах от блюда шел такой, что рот пса немедленно наполнился жидкой слюной.
reading.question: How does the dog react to the smell coming from the covered silver dish?
options: His mouth immediately fills with drool
He runs away from the smell
He falls asleep
He barks angrily at Zina
reading.correct: His mouth immediately fills with drool
reading.explain: The smell from the dish is so strong that the dog's mouth instantly fills with saliva.

reading.ru: Дарья Петровна сама отлично готовит водку.
reading.question: According to Filipp Filippovich, who makes excellent vodka?
options: Darya Petrovna makes it herself
It is bought from a shop on the Arbat
Doctor Barmental distills it
Zina brings it from the market
reading.correct: Darya Petrovna makes it herself
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich explains that what they are drinking is spirit, because Darya Petrovna herself makes excellent vodka.

reading.ru: Заметьте, Иван Арнольдович, холодными закусками и супом закусывают только недорезанные большевиками помещики.
reading.question: According to Filipp Filippovich, who eats cold appetizers and soup as a meal?
options: Only landowners the Bolsheviks failed to finish off
Only doctors and professors
Only the working class
Only foreigners visiting Moscow
reading.correct: Only landowners the Bolsheviks failed to finish off
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich claims only half-slaughtered landowners left over from the Bolsheviks eat cold snacks and soup as their main course.

reading.ru: Пес сидел в тени скатерти с видом часового у порохового склада, а Филипп Филиппович, заложив хвост тугой салфетки за воротничок, проповедовал.
reading.question: What is the dog doing while Filipp Filippovich lectures at dinner?
options: Sitting in the shadow of the tablecloth like a sentry at a powder magazine
Sleeping under the table
Barking at the guests
Eating from a bowl in the kitchen
reading.correct: Sitting in the shadow of the tablecloth like a sentry at a powder magazine
reading.explain: The dog sits in the shade of the tablecloth 'with the air of a sentry at a powder magazine' while the professor lectures.

reading.ru: Вы знаете, я произвел 30 наблюдений у себя в клинике.
reading.question: What experiment does Filipp Filippovich say he conducted in his clinic?
options: Thirty observations on patients related to reading newspapers
Thirty surgeries on stray dogs
Thirty tests of different vodka brands
Thirty interviews with committee members
reading.correct: Thirty observations on patients related to reading newspapers
reading.explain: He mentions having made thirty observations at his clinic, comparing patients who read Soviet newspapers to those who did not.

reading.ru: Псу достался бледный и толстый кусок осетрины, который ему не понравилось, а непосредственно за ним ломоть окровавленного Ростбифа.
reading.question: What food does the dog get during the meal, and which part does he dislike?
options: A pale sturgeon fillet he dislikes, followed by bloody roast beef
A bowl of porridge he loves
Only bread crusts
Raw fish he refuses entirely
reading.correct: A pale sturgeon fillet he dislikes, followed by bloody roast beef
reading.explain: The dog receives a pale, fat piece of sturgeon which he doesn't like, then immediately after, a slice of bloody roast beef.

reading.ru: Глухой, смягченный потолками и коврами, хорал, донесся откуда-то сверху и сбоку.
reading.question: What sound does the dog hear, muffled by the ceilings and carpets?
options: A choral singing coming from somewhere above and to the side
A dog barking outside
A telephone ringing
Glass breaking
reading.correct: A choral singing coming from somewhere above and to the side
reading.explain: A muffled chorus, softened by ceilings and carpets, drifts in from somewhere above and to the side — the tenants' meeting singing.

reading.ru: С 1903 года я живу в этом доме.
reading.question: Since what year does Filipp Filippovich say he has lived in this house?
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich states he has lived in this house since 1903 as part of his argument about the galoshes stand.

reading.ru: В марте 17-го в один прекрасный день пропали все калоши.
reading.question: What happened to all the galoshes in the building in March 1917?
options: They all disappeared in a single day
They were all repaired
They were donated to the poor
They were replaced with new ones
reading.correct: They all disappeared in a single day
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich recounts that in March 1917 all the galoshes in the entryway vanished in one fine day, along with canes, a coat, and a samovar.

reading.ru: На нём есть теперь калоши и эти калоши…  мои!
reading.question: What does Filipp Filippovich claim about Sharikov's (the committee member's) galoshes?
options: That they are actually his own stolen galoshes
That they are brand new from a shop
That they belong to Doctor Barmental
That they were a gift from Darya Petrovna
reading.correct: That they are actually his own stolen galoshes
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich declares the galoshes the man is wearing now are his own — the very ones that disappeared in 1917.

reading.ru: Почему электричество, которое, дай бог памяти, тухло в течение 20 лет два раза, в теперешнее время аккуратно гаснет раз в месяц?
reading.question: What complaint does Filipp Filippovich make about the electricity?
options: That it now regularly goes out once a month, unlike in the past 20 years
That it has never worked at all
That it is too expensive
That it was recently installed and is unreliable
reading.correct: That it now regularly goes out once a month, unlike in the past 20 years
reading.explain: He complains that electricity which barely failed twice in twenty years now reliably goes out once a month.

reading.ru: Следовательно, разруха не в клозетах, а в головах.
reading.question: What is Filipp Filippovich's famous conclusion about the cause of 'devastation' (разруха)?
options: That the devastation is in people's heads, not in the toilets
That the devastation is caused by foreign spies
That the devastation does not exist at all
That the devastation is caused by the weather
reading.correct: That the devastation is in people's heads, not in the toilets
reading.explain: His famous line concludes that 'devastation' is not in the plumbing but in people's heads.

reading.ru: Его слова на сонного пса падали точно глухой подземный гул.
reading.question: How do Filipp Filippovich's words affect the drowsy dog?
options: They fall on him like a dull underground rumble
They wake him up completely
They make him bark loudly
They have no effect on him
reading.correct: They fall on him like a dull underground rumble
reading.explain: The professor's words fall on the sleepy dog like a dull, muffled underground rumble as he drifts off.

reading.ru: Во-первых, кролик издох, а во-вторых, сегодня в Большом Аида.
reading.question: Why does Filipp Filippovich say he won't need the doctor's help that evening?
options: Because the rabbit died, and also there is a performance of Aida at the Bolshoi
Because he is going on vacation
Because he is too tired to work
Because the clinic is closed for repairs
reading.correct: Because the rabbit died, and also there is a performance of Aida at the Bolshoi
reading.explain: He explains that firstly the rabbit has died, and secondly, Aida is playing at the Bolshoi tonight, which he loves.

reading.ru: В течение недели пес сожрал столько же, сколько в полтора последних голодных месяца на улице.
reading.question: How much did the dog eat in his first week with the professor, compared to his life on the street?
options: As much as in his last month and a half of hunger on the street
Almost nothing, since he refused all food
The same amount as any ordinary week
Less than he used to eat on the street
reading.correct: As much as in his last month and a half of hunger on the street
reading.explain: In a single week at the apartment, the dog ate as much as he had in his last month and a half of hunger on the streets.

reading.ru: Чем тебе помешала сова, хулиган?
reading.question: What does Filipp Filippovich scold the dog about regarding the stuffed owl?
options: Why he attacked and destroyed the owl for no reason
Why he was afraid of the owl
Why he brought the owl a gift
Why he ignored the owl completely
reading.correct: Why he attacked and destroyed the owl for no reason
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich demands to know what the stuffed owl ever did to bother him, calling him a hooligan for tearing it apart.

reading.ru: На следующий день на пса надели широкий блестящий ошейник.
reading.question: What happens to the dog the day after the owl incident?
options: He is fitted with a wide, shiny collar
He is thrown out of the apartment
He is taken to a veterinarian
He is given a new name
reading.correct: He is fitted with a wide, shiny collar
reading.explain: The next day the dog is put into a wide, shiny collar, which at first upsets him deeply.

reading.ru: Когда пересекали трамвайные рельсы, милиционер посмотрел на ошейник с удовольствием и уважением.
reading.question: How does the policeman react when he sees the dog's new collar?
options: He looks at it with pleasure and respect
He tries to confiscate it
He laughs at the dog
He ignores it completely
reading.correct: He looks at it with pleasure and respect
reading.explain: As they cross the tram tracks, a policeman glances at the collar with evident pleasure and respect.

reading.ru: Всякий день в черной и сверху облицованной кафелем плите стреляло и бушевало пламя.
reading.question: What is happening in Darya Petrovna's kitchen every day?
options: Flames crackle and rage in the black, tile-topped stove
The stove is cold and unused
Water is constantly boiling over
The kitchen is being renovated
reading.correct: Flames crackle and rage in the black, tile-topped stove
reading.explain: Every day the black stove, faced with tile on top, crackles and rages with flame in Darya Petrovna's kitchen.

reading.ru: В модной прическе на уши и с корзинкой светлых волос на затылке светились 22 поддельных бриллианта.
reading.question: What detail is mentioned about Darya Petrovna's fashionable hairstyle?
options: Twenty-two fake diamonds glittered in it
It was completely covered by a cap
It was recently shaved off
It had flowers woven into it
reading.correct: Twenty-two fake diamonds glittered in it
reading.explain: Her fashionable hairstyle, with a basket of light hair at the back, glitters with twenty-two imitation diamonds.

reading.ru: В окне кухни над белой половинной занавесочкой стояла густая и важная Причистинская ночь с одинокой звездой.
reading.question: What can be seen through the kitchen window at night?
options: A thick, solemn Prechistenka night with a single star
Bright city lights and traffic
Nothing, since the window is boarded up
A view of the Bolshoi Theatre
reading.correct: A thick, solemn Prechistenka night with a single star
reading.explain: Above the half-curtain of the kitchen window hangs the thick, dignified Prechistenka night, with a lone star.

reading.ru: В отвратительной, едкой и мутной жиже в стеклянных сосудах лежали человеческие мозги.
reading.question: What does the dog observe in the glass vessels in the professor's study?
options: Human brains lying in a foul, murky liquid
Preserved flowers
Bottles of vodka
Small fish
reading.correct: Human brains lying in a foul, murky liquid
reading.explain: In the disgusting, caustic, murky liquid inside glass vessels lie human brains, which the dog watches the professor examine.

reading.ru: Проходя по коридору, пёс услышал, как в кабинете Филиппа Филипповича неприятно и неожиданно прозвенел телефон.
reading.question: What interrupts the calm evening as the dog passes through the corridor?
options: The telephone rings unpleasantly and unexpectedly in the study
Someone knocks loudly at the front door
A window shatters
Darya Petrovna starts singing
reading.correct: The telephone rings unpleasantly and unexpectedly in the study
reading.explain: As the dog walks down the corridor, he hears the telephone in Filipp Filippovich's study ring unpleasantly and unexpectedly.

reading.ru: Тот привез с собой дурно пахнущий чемодан и, даже не раздеваясь, устремился с ним через коридор в смотровую.
reading.question: What does Doctor Barmental do the moment he arrives after the phone call?
options: He rushes with a foul-smelling suitcase straight to the examination room, without even taking off his coat
He sits down to have dinner first
He calls the police
He goes to sleep, saying it can wait
reading.correct: He rushes with a foul-smelling suitcase straight to the examination room, without even taking off his coat
reading.explain: Barmental arrives with a bad-smelling suitcase and, without even undressing, rushes with it through the corridor to the examination room.

reading.ru: Затем весь мир перевернулся дном к верху И была еще почувствована холодная, но приятная рука под животом.
reading.question: What is the dog's last sensation as he loses consciousness under the anesthetic at the end of the chapter?
options: The world turning upside down, and a cold but pleasant hand under his belly
A loud explosion
The taste of sausage
Bright sunlight
reading.correct: The world turning upside down, and a cold but pleasant hand under his belly
reading.explain: As the anesthetic takes full effect, the whole world turns upside down for the dog, and he feels one last cold but pleasant hand beneath his stomach.

highlight.question: How did the dog react to the smell of the food Zina brought in?
sentences: Зина внесла серебряное крытое блюдо, в котором что-то ворчало.
Запах от блюда шёл такой, что рот пса немедленно наполнился жидкой слюной.
– подумал он и застучал по паркету хвостом, как палкой.
highlight.explain: His mouth immediately filled with drool at the smell, and he excitedly beat his tail on the floor like a stick.

highlight.question: What did Filipp Filippovich conclude from his newspaper observations?
sentences: Вы знаете, я произвёл 30 наблюдений у себя в клинике.
Пациенты, не читающие газет, чувствуют себя превосходно.
Те же, которых я специально заставлял читать «Правду», – теряли в весе.
highlight.explain: Patients who avoided reading newspapers felt excellent, while those he forced to read Pravda lost weight.

highlight.question: What was Filipp Filippovich suggesting about the causes of social problems?
sentences: Буржуй Саблин?  (Филипп Филиппович ткнул пальцем в потолок).
highlight.explain: He suggested it was absurd to believe that ordinary businessmen could be driving social change.

highlight.question: What were his reasons for canceling work that day?
sentences: Во-первых, кролик издох, а во-вторых, сегодня в большом – «Аида».
highlight.explain: The rabbit had died, and besides, the opera Aida was being performed at the theater that evening.

highlight.question: What demonstrated how completely the dog had become attached to Filipp Filippovich?
sentences: В течение недели пёс сожрал столько же, сколько в полтора последних голодных месяца на улице.
О качестве еды у Филиппа Филипповича и говорить не приходилось.

Если даже не принимать во внимание того, что ежедневно Дарьей Петровной закупалась груда обрезков на Смоленском рынке на 18 копеек, достаточно упомянуть обеды в 7 часов вечера в столовой, на которых пёс присутствовал, несмотря на протесты изящной Зины.
Во время этих обедов Филипп Филиппович окончательно получил звание божества.
Пёс становился на задние лапы и жевал пиджак, пёс изучил звонок Филиппа Филипповича – два полнозвучных отрывистых хозяйских удара, и вылетал с лаем встречать его в передней.

Хозяин вваливался в чернобурой лисе, сверкая миллионом снежных блёсток, пахнущий мандаринами, сигарами, духами, лимонами, бензином, одеколоном, сукном, и голос его, как командная труба, разносился по всему жилищу.
highlight.explain: The dog learned his master's distinctive bell, ran barking to greet him in the hallway, and stood on hind legs to chew his jacket.

highlight.question: What was the dog claiming about his position in the household?
sentences: – и он боком лез в дверь, просовывая в неё морду.
highlight.explain: By pointing out his collar and insisting he was no pickpocket, the dog was asserting he belonged there and was not a street vagabond.
